perspectivesWordKit.definition: absolutely necessary for something
perspectivesWordKit.example: Exposure to diverse perspectives is indispensable to developing critical thinking.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: ignored; treated as unimportant
perspectivesWordKit.example: Minority viewpoints are often disregarded in public debate.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: too great to be overcome
perspectivesWordKit.example: Cultural differences are rarely an insurmountable barrier to understanding.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to make stronger, louder or more intense
perspectivesWordKit.example: Social media can amplify a single perspective until it drowns out all others.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to improve the quality or value of something
perspectivesWordKit.example: Studying abroad can enhance one’s ability to see an issue from several angles.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to encourage the development of something
perspectivesWordKit.example: Schools should foster open discussion between students with opposing views.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: a hidden danger or common mistake
perspectivesWordKit.example: A common pitfall of relying on one news source is confirmation bias.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to feel familiar or meaningful to someone
perspectivesWordKit.example: Personal stories tend to resonate with readers more deeply than statistics.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: easily influenced or harmed (+ to)
perspectivesWordKit.example: Teenagers are particularly susceptible to the opinions of their peers.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: the ability to do or understand something
perspectivesWordKit.example: Empathy expands our capacity to understand people unlike ourselves.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: strongly advised or encouraged
perspectivesWordKit.example: Experts have urged teachers to show students how to evaluate competing viewpoints.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to dare to go or say something risky; a risky project
perspectivesWordKit.example: Few people venture beyond the comfort of their own opinions.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: disagreement with an official or widely accepted view
perspectivesWordKit.example: A healthy society tolerates dissidence rather than silencing it.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: honest and direct
perspectivesWordKit.example: A candid exchange of views reveals assumptions we did not know we held.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: laziness; doing nothing
perspectivesWordKit.example: Intellectual idleness leads people to accept the first opinion they hear.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to gradually put an idea or feeling into someone
perspectivesWordKit.example: Parents should instill in children respect for views different from their own.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to represent or express an idea in a visible form
perspectivesWordKit.example: Great literature can embody the perspective of people from another era.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: slightly worried or uncomfortable
perspectivesWordKit.example: Meeting a very different worldview can make us feel uneasy at first.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: creating tension about what will happen
perspectivesWordKit.example: The novel’s suspenseful plot is told from three alternating perspectives.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: making you feel anxious or disturbed
perspectivesWordKit.example: It is unsettling to realise that our beliefs depend on where we were born.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: emotionally distant; objective
perspectivesWordKit.example: A detached observer may judge a conflict more fairly than those involved.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: finding something funny
perspectivesWordKit.example: Some readers were amused by the satire, while others were deeply offended.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: cheerful and not serious
perspectivesWordKit.example: A lighthearted tone can make a controversial idea easier to accept.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: great enthusiasm for something
perspectivesWordKit.example: Her zeal for debate pushed her to read authors she disagreed with.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: continuing without becoming weaker
perspectivesWordKit.example: Despite decades of research, the debate continues unabated.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: worried that something bad may happen
perspectivesWordKit.example: Many people are apprehensive about sharing unpopular opinions online.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: the ability to manage without help from others
perspectivesWordKit.example: Intellectual self-sufficiency should not become an excuse for ignoring others.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: a feeling that someone or something is worthless
perspectivesWordKit.example: Treating opposing opinions with contempt shuts down dialogue.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: letting some light through, not fully clear
perspectivesWordKit.example: Our perspective is like translucent glass: it lets the world in but colours everything.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: suffering from something bad (+ by/with)
perspectivesWordKit.example: Societies afflicted by polarisation struggle to find common ground.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to tell someone confidently so they stop doubting
perspectivesWordKit.example: I can assure the reader that listening to both sides does not mean giving up your own.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: only; and nothing else
perspectivesWordKit.example: Forming opinions solely from headlines is a dangerous habit.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: the ability to adapt to many situations
perspectivesWordKit.example: The versatility to switch perspectives is a mark of a mature thinker.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: deeply involving all your senses or attention
perspectivesWordKit.example: Immersive experiences such as living abroad transform how we see our own culture.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to communicate an idea or feeling
perspectivesWordKit.example: Art can convey a perspective that words alone cannot.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: to develop or become clear gradually
perspectivesWordKit.example: As the story unfolds, the reader begins to sympathise with the villain.

perspectivesWordKit.definition: complete; including all parts
perspectivesWordKit.example: A comprehensive understanding of any issue requires hearing every side.
